emma: Hey team — customer tenant `acme-inc` hit 0 credits around 02:05 UTC and reported their product went read-only. They say they were only doing a short burst from a nightly job, but CI logs show ~1.2M tokens in a 3-minute window. Can someone confirm the reset window and whether bursts are throttled differently for reserved accounts?

raj: pulling logs. which plan is acme on?

emma: Dedicated, monthly commit. They show usage spikes on 2026-03-10 02:01:36 -> 02:04:40 UTC. UI shows zero until the tenant reset at 00:00 local tz? customer is PST (America/Los_Angeles).

matt: Dedicated monthly commits don't roll over. Reset timing is account-local midnight by billing timezone, but backend enforcement uses UTC-based windows for burst accounting in some legacy cases. we'll verify for this tenant.

quota-bot: NOTE: Automated alert — tenant acme-inc exceeded burst threshold (burst_window=300s, threshold=1e6 tokens) at 2145675600. Throttles applied.

raj: I see two things in the traces: (1) a large continuous request stream that bypassed client-side batching (2) cache inconsistency — the token-balance cache for tenant snapshots had a TTL of 30s and we saw a 7-minute stale read during the refill.

emma: so why did their UI show zero for hours? they said credits "didn't come back" after midnight PST.

raj: probable sequence: backend reset processed at tenant's midnight (08:00 UTC) -> token ledger updated -> API gateway cache still served the old zero-balance for 7m due to a mis-synchronization with the billing event. normally TTL 30s. that explains minutes, not hours. what timezone is the customer expecting?

emma: customer says their team waited ~3 hours.

matt: log excerpt (billing job):
```
2026-03-10T08:00:02Z INFO billing.reset tenant=acme-inc new_balance=500000 commit=dedicated_monthly
2026-03-10T08:00:03Z INFO billing.notify-cache tenant=acme-inc event=balance_updated
```

raj: gateway logs: repeated cache GET hits for tenant snapshot returning balance=0 from 08:00:04Z -> 08:07:32Z. then a purge and subsequent GET returned balance=500000. After that, we saw a second consumer spike that consumed most of the reopened balance within 10m.

emma: aaah — so they got refilled but then immediately consumed by some background tasks? customer says they only ran one job.

raj: could be another service account under the org. I can list token-consuming principals for that interval.

matt: action items: (1) confirm exact refill timestamp in billing ledger (we have 08:00:02Z) (2) export consumption per API key between 08:00-08:20Z (3) check gateway cache TTL metrics and reconcile why it was 7m for this tenant.

emma: customer-facing response proposal: explain reset boundary (account timezone), note we observed a cache propagation delay causing a visible UI lag of ~7m, and show consumption after refill. offer temporary top-up while we audit. ok?

raj: yep. I'll generate per-key usage and flag any service accounts.

matt: i'll handle the top-up approval. please include repro steps for us to prevent regen: steps to reproduce (what I would add to the thread):
1) set tenant timezone to America/Los_Angeles in staging
2) seed tenant with X credits and a background job that fires at 23:59:30 local tz producing a rapid token stream (~1M tokens over 3m)
3) trigger billing reset at 00:00 local tz and observe gateway cache behavior and token ledger update times
4) measure UI refresh and cache TTLs

emma: customer asked if we throttle bursts differently for Dedicated vs Hosted. short answer?

raj: Dedicated tenants have higher burst ceilings, but the enforcement path still goes through the same gateway rate limiters. There are platform-level burst guards (soft and hard). Soft guards allow temporary overage visible as throttling/warnings; hard guards will cut requests. In this case, we hit a soft guard then ledger went to zero.

emma: final support reply drafted: "We investigated: your tenant's monthly quota reset executed at 00:00 in your account timezone (PST) and our billing ledger shows the balance update at 2026-03-10T08:00:02Z. We observed a short cache propagation delay (approx 7 minutes) that caused the UI to show zero until the gateway cache was purged; after the balance update the tenant's keys were quickly consumed by additional requests, which depleted the replenished tokens. We're continuing to audit which API key(s) consumed the tokens. We've issued a one-time emergency top-up (50k tokens) while we complete the investigation. Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with per-key logs and a mitigation plan to avoid long UI delays during resets." sound good?

matt: fine by me. include offer for a post-mortem if they'd like.

raj: adding note: engineering will add a guard to ensure cache TTLs for billing-critical keys are <=60s and add a short push invalidation on ledger updates to avoid >30s staleness.

emma: thanks. I'll send to customer and mark ticket as escalated.

matt: /remind me to follow up on the top-up reconciliation tomorrow :calendar:
